editorial.headline: Fee-Based Real-Estate Services, Open Nationally and Unblocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: From rent collection to non-residential property management and transaction advice, this fee- or contract-based real-estate activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership and not blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 68299 covers real-estate services supplied for a fee or under another contractual arrangement. Its scope includes rent-collection agencies; the management of non-residential real estate, including jointly owned non-residential property; and paid consulting connected with the purchase, sale and leasing of real estate. It also reaches other forms of real-estate provision delivered on a fee or contract basis. The common thread is service work around real estate carried out for remuneration or contract: collecting rent, managing non-residential property, advising on purchase, sale and leasing, or providing another included real-estate service.

That framing matters when deciding whether this is the right activity to register. The record makes it available at every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. It presents the same scope alongside all four scales. For a registrant, the activity description turns on the work actually being carried out—rent collection, non-residential real-estate management, consulting around transactions or leasing, or another fee- or contract-based real-estate service within the stated scope.

Nationally, the PMA position is plain in the record: status TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In ownership terms, that permits full foreign ownership for this activity. The national PMA source cited is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That national position sits alongside the broad scale availability, from Mikro through Besar, without changing the defined service scope.

Bali is also clear, though for a different reason. The Bali assessment gives the status OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and does not mark the activity as blocked. At Besar scale, the stated OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi—Medium-High/High—which is why the activity is not caught by the moratorium. The applicable Bali rule is island-wide and permanent and blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk activities. This activity falls outside that prohibition in the supplied assessment. For a foreign investor, the candid conclusion is simple: the national 100% ceiling carries into a Bali position that is not blocked by this moratorium.
